title: Philadelphia (Revelation 3:7–13)
hookLine: little strength, but an open door no one can shut

cards: "Thou hast a little strength." An odd line for a letter of praise. Not great strength, not hidden reserves.
A little. That's what the risen Christ says to the church in Philadelphia, and not as a scolding. In the same breath he tells them a door has been set open in front of them, and nobody can shut it.
A small church, low on strength, in front of a door it didn't open and can't be locked out of. It's the week's end, so the letters so far get a look back too.

teach.b: First, who's speaking: "he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth."
It echoes Isaiah, where a steward is handed the key of the house of David: "so he shall open, and none shall shut." The key isn't the church's.

teach.h: A LITTLE STRENGTH, AN OPEN DOOR.
teach.b: Second, the door: "behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name." The door isn't a prize for being strong.

It's set open for people with a little strength who kept going. What the door is, readers differ. Some hear a door for sharing the gospel, as Paul writes that "a great door and effectual is opened unto me."
Others hear the door into God's kingdom.

teach.h: A PILLAR THAT GOES NO MORE OUT.
teach.b: Third, a promise for people who feel small: "Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out." A pillar holds a building up and never gets moved out. Fourth, the week.
It opened on Patmos with fear not. Ephesus was asked to return to its first love. Smyrna, poor but rich, was promised a crown of life.
Pergamum got a white stone and a new name. Thyatira grew, more than at first. Sardis was told to wake up.
Philadelphia, with its little strength, got a door.

teach.h: A WEEK OF LETTERS: I KNOW THY WORKS.
teach.b: In the King James text, each letter turns to its church with the same words: I know thy works. Someone is paying attention to these churches.

how: Christians sometimes speak of an 'open door' when a new chance to serve or to share their faith appears, borrowing the language of Revelation 3:8 and of Paul's letters.

games.q: you're in a small church with a little strength. a door has been set open in front of you. what does the letter say about it?
o: you'll need more strength before you can use it.
it will close soon, so hurry.
games.why: "I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength." the door is for the small, not the strong.

practice: If you can, step slowly through the nearest doorway, noticing the frame and the air on each side; if you can't move right now, walk through a familiar door in your mind.
Then ask: what door is already open in my life that I've been waiting to feel strong enough for? If you pray, name it to God; if not, just hold it.
